item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump offered Americans a first look at the newly regilded Arts of War sculptures in Washington, D.C., as crews began removing the towering scaffolding that concealed the iconic golden horses during months of restoration work.

"Taking down the scaffolding around the regilded Arts of War sculptures!" Trump wrote on Truth Social, sharing photographs of workers carefully dismantling the structure surrounding the massive monument near the Lincoln Memorial.

Exclusive Fox News video captured workers removing the final sections of scaffolding, revealing the gleaming gold horses and figures that crown the monumental granite pedestals.

The Arts of War sculptures flank the eastern entrance to Arlington Memorial Bridge just west of the Lincoln Memorial, while their companion Arts of Peace sculptures sit nearby along Parkway Drive. Each monument features gilded bronze horses and human figures mounted atop massive granite bases, according to a study by MTFA Design.

TOP TRUMP OFFICIAL TOUTS HOW DC MAKEOVER IS PROOF AMERICA IS REJECTING 'DECLINE BY CHOICE'

The restoration is part of an ongoing National Park Service preservation project. According to the same 2018 study, the granite pedestals had developed extensive purple staining caused by copper runoff from the aging bronze sculptures, prompting specialized cleaning and stabilization work in addition to regilding.

The agency temporarily closed surrounding lawn and turf areas beginning July 2 to protect visitors, workers and the historic monuments while construction continues. The restrictions are scheduled to remain in effect through Sept. 30, though the National Park Service said areas will reopen as soon as the work no longer requires them to remain closed.

‘DERANGED’ VANDALS FUEL MALL SABOTAGE TREND, FROM BLOOD WRITING TO REFLECTING POOL DAMAGE

Sidewalks bordering the restoration area and those leading onto Memorial Bridge remain accessible, and the project has not required any road closures, according to the agency.

The surrounding parkland will remain partially restricted while crews complete the broader rehabilitation project and remove the remaining construction equipment.

For months, the towering monuments were almost entirely hidden behind scaffolding, tarps and fencing. 

Trump's photos and Fox News' exclusive video now offer one of the clearest looks yet at the restored sculptures are unveiled with a renewed gold finish just in time for America's 250th anniversary.

The White House did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

item.title: Sudan's forgotten war leaves millions hungry as global attention remains elsewhere
item.description: El Fasher and El Obeid remain flashpoints as UN reports detail war crimes, mass rape, and genocide conditions in Sudan's escalating civil war.
item.content:encoded:
As multiple international crises grip the world, from Iran to Russia’s war in Ukraine, Sudan quietly remains one of the largest humanitarian and displacement disasters in the world.

Since the outbreak of hostilities in 2023, over 14 million people have been displaced and nearly 34 million people are in desperate need of humanitarian support, accounting for 10% of global needs, according to the International Rescue Committee.

"The war in Sudan has caused the world's largest humanitarian crisis and has escalated into a regional war involving all of its neighbors as well as numerous Middle Eastern powers," Alan Boswell, Project Director for the Horn of Africa at International Crisis Group, told Fox News Digital.

"Despite this, world leaders continue to ignore the conflict, leaving it to subordinates. That approach continues to fail," Boswell added.

COULD THIS AFRICAN NATION BECOME TRUMP'S NEXT TERROR TARGET AS JIHADISTS CLOSE IN ON POWER?

The United Nations says that some 19.5 million people are experiencing acute hunger, and 4.5 million people have fled the country.

The U.S. also recently imposed an additional round of sanctions against the Sudanese Armed Forces for allegedly using chemical weapons in 2024 in violations of the Chemical Weapons Convention.

The Sudanese government denied the allegations.

The Trump administration has made significant efforts in trying to mediate between Russia and Ukraine, as well as bring Israel’s war against Gaza to an end. The administration is also trying to uphold a shaky ceasefire that was agreed with Iran to halt the war that began on February 28.

"For three years, we have warned that Sudan was on the brink of catastrophe, and those warnings have gone unanswered," said International Rescue Committee Country Director Richard Data.

Sudan’s recent outbreak of civil war, following years of coups and credible accusations of ethnic cleansing and genocide, persists under the radar.

TRUMP ADMINISTRATION TOUTS MORE THAN $1B IN UN BUDGET CUTS AS REFORM PUSH GAINS MOMENTUM

The civil war broke out in April 2023 between the Sudanese Armed Forces led by Gen. Abdel Fattah al-Burhan and Gen. Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, widely known as "Hemedti," leader of the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF).

The two had been in an uneasy alliance ruling the country following the 2019 overthrow of Sudan’s longtime dictator, Omar al-Bashir, who had been in power since 1989. Together, the generals staged another coup in 2021, toppling the interim civilian government that had been in power after the fall of Bashir.

While both the Sudanese Armed Forces and RSF are accused of committing atrocities, recent reports have highlighted the brutality of the RSF.

A major focus of the deteriorating conditions has been in El-Obeid in North Kordofan state, where an escalating hunger crisis is plaguing over 100,000 displaced people in camps throughout the city.

"What we need to do is really now to plan for the scale-up beyond the 100,000 people that we have been supporting," said World Food Programme Sudan Country Director, Abdallah Alwardat.

El Fasher in the Darfur region is another major flashpoint, where the RSF took control in October 2025 and killed more than 6,000 people in the initial siege of the city.

A recent July report from the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights revealed widespread acts of sexual violence against women and girls, some as young as 12, including reports of mass and gang rapes committed by the RSF.

The RSF is also accused of abduction, with survivors describing incidents of girls and women being beaten, having their hands tied behind their backs, and being driven away in a Land cruiser.

The United Nations and other human rights groups have accused the RSF of perpetrating ethnically targeted attacks and concluded that at least three components of genocide have been overwhelmingly met, including deliberately inflicting conditions of life intended to destroy a group in whole or in part.

A U.N. report from September 2025 found that the Sudanese Armed Forces have also committed war crimes and attacked civilian populations and infrastructure. Both the Sudanese Armed Forces and the Rapid Support Forces targeted civilians with perceived affiliations to the enemy, executing, torturing and raping victims.

item.title: The WNBA team that mocked Sophie Cunningham can barely win a game, Tony Romo limbers up & MLB's Abby Labar!
item.description: Sophie Cunningham's women's sports stance sparks a response from the 6-24 Seattle Storm as Stefanie Dolson wears a trans rights shirt in protest.
item.content:encoded:
'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday–Friday on OutKick.com.

Final Hump Day of July. Can you believe it?

All 32 NFL teams have reported. We've already had at least one brawl in camp. Tua's already hurt. Players are holding out. Players are "holding in" (figure that one out).

It's all happening, folks, and ...

The insufferable WNBA is again front and center.

Credit where it's due — they're stealing headlines. Perhaps that's the goal? I'm not sure it's the best strategy given that cultish league becomes uglier and uglier with each passing day, but hey, bad PR is still PR.

WNBA STAR SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM'S PLAYER EXCLUSIVE ADIDAS SHOE SELLS OUT IN LESS THAN AN HOUR ONLINE

Welcome to a Hump Day Nightcaps — the one where Sophie Cunningham continues to melt brains, this time out west! That's right.

For those of you who thought Seattle was full of crazies, you ain't seen nothing yet!

What else? I've got new Tony Romo bodycam footage from his OWI over the weekend, the Mets' broadcasters being absolutely DISGUSTED by the Atlanta Braves, and MLB Network's Abby Labar checks in to end the day.

TONY ROMO TREATING HIS FIELD SOBRIETY TEST LIKE AN NFL COMBINE LEAVES FANS STUNNED

Sound good? Good!

Grab you some chicken wings for National Chicken Wing Day, and settle in for a Hump Day 'Cap!

First of all, blue cheese is the best dipping sauce for chicken wings. That's probably an unpopular opinion, but it's the correct one. Ranch is certainly more versatile, but blue cheese owns chicken wings.

Another unpopular opinion? Dry rub is the way to go. Give me the dipping sauce on the side. Buffalo wings are great. Garlic Parmesan wings are terrific. But give me those sauces on the side.

It's cleaner and, frankly, it tastes better. You get a better bite. The little game you play at a restaurant between eating the wings, wiping your hands, and drinking your beer is exhausting. It's too much. Doesn't happen if the wings are naked. It's just better.

Most things in life are.

And that's your Ted Talk for the day!

Now, let's get this class started with the Seattle Storm — who sit at a whopping 6-24 after last night's loss to Indiana — being just the most insufferable "professional" sports team on the planet (this week, at least):

The WNBA is such an embarrassing league. It's a cult. It's an activist group. It's so backwards, it's almost unbelievable.

Almost.

This Seattle Storm player, Stefanie Dolson, decided to try and make a name for herself by wearing a "Trans Rights Are Human Rights" shirt, and it's just so pathetic.

Sophie Cunningham never said trans rights weren't human rights, dummies. She said biological men don't belong in women's sports. That's a stark difference. It's something that, up until a few years ago, NEVER needed to be said because it was a laughable thought.

Of course they don't belong! Duh.

But the narrative shifted a few years back, and it's been a Culture War ever since. A dumb one, of course, but a war nonetheless.

PS: Let's go ahead and check in on the all-inclusive Seattle Storm's season:

Whoaaaaaaaaa Nellie! 6-24! Way to go, Storm. Worst team in the WNBA. 1-14 in the conference. Currently on a 7-game skid. Losers of nine of their last 10 games.

And THIS is the team that's attacking Sophie Cunningham? Okeedokee.

Unserious league. Serious cult.

Next? Let's head on out to Wisconsin, where Tony Romo failed his sobriety test last weekend despite going through all the proper warm-up techniques:

"Sorry, two back surgeries, I need to stand here."

Just PEAK TV from Tony Romo in that parking garage. I've given him a lot of crap over the years for his shtick in the booth, but this reeled me right back in. I've never seen a man get down on start to stretch like he's about to run the 40 before a sobriety test. Never in my life.

Credit to Romo for giving it his all, though. Some folks mail it in. Not Romo. If he's going to start a task, he's going to try and do it to the best of his ability. That's what four-time Pro Bowl quarterbacks do.

You play to win the game. A great man once said that, and it's true in all facets of life — not just sports. Romo's back was against the wall here after being stuffed in the back of a tiny police car on the drive over, and he needed to work up a quick sweat to get the juices flowing before the lights came on.

PS: This Romo stuff forced me to do some Big J digging on Wisconsin DUI laws, and they are stunning. Did y'all know that A) it's referred to as an "OWI" only in Wisconsin, and B) it's basically a slap on the wrist for the first THREE offenses?

That's right. In fact, the penalty for a first offense is a small fine ($150-300) and your license is revoked for a few months. That's pretty much it.

Wild state.

OK, let's rapid-fire this Hump Day class into a big Hump Day Night. First up? Where do we stand on the Braves letting this poor minor league kid get absolutely rocked the other night?

Goodness gracious. It's tough to watch. I get it, but it's tough to watch. You have to feel at least a little bad for Connor Thomas.

It does beg the question ... when is enough enough? The Braves put in a position player right after him. Why not just do it earlier? What difference does it make at that point? You have plenty of position players. Can't one of them just go out there and throw BP for an hour rather than shatter this kid's confidence?

For those wondering what giving up 11 runs and walking five over 2.2 innings looks like on the stat sheet, Thomas is now 0-1 this season with a 21.32 ERA. He was sent back down to Gwinnett after the game.

He probably couldn't get on that plane fast enough.

Next? I've got a ONE MONTH warning for all you dads out there with summer chores still not checked off ...

Look at that ... it's beautiful. What a Week 0 slate!

Chills. We're so close. One month, folks. Get that yard work DONE and ready for the fall over these next three weekends. Thank me later.

OK, that's it for today. Solid Hump Day, everyone. I think we did well.

MLB Network's Abby Labar takes us into the second half of the week!

Would the Storm have more than six wins if they had a biological man on their team? Email me at Zach.Dean@OutKick.com.

item.title: Violent anti-ICE rioter who targeted police finally faces reckoning in federal court
item.description: A 42-year-old Los Angeles man was sentenced to 37 months in federal prison for targeting law enforcement during violent anti-ICE protests on a highway overpass.
item.content:encoded:
A California man accused of taking part in a violent confrontation during last year's anti-ICE riots in Los Angeles was sentenced to more than three years in federal prison after admitting he targeted law enforcement officers caught in the chaos.

Ismael Vega, 42, of Los Angeles' Westlake neighborhood was sentenced Monday to 37 months in prison and ordered to pay $253,415 in restitution for his role in the June 8, 2025, attack, the Justice Department announced.

"Those who attack our brave officers protecting public safety will face federal prison time for their crimes," U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli wrote Monday on X after the sentencing. "Let this be a warning to others who think they can act without consequences."

Vega pleaded guilty in April to obstructing, impeding and interfering with law enforcement during civil disorder.

FBI ARRESTS PROTESTER WHO THREATENED TO KILL ICE OFFICER'S FAMILY AT NJ DETENTION CENTER PROTEST, BLANCHE SAYS

According to court documents, Vega was among a large crowd gathered on the Main Street overpass above U.S. Highway 101 as protests over federal immigration enforcement descended into violence.

Prosecutors said Vega knew California Highway Patrol officers were trapped beneath the overpass when rioters began dropping burning debris, fireworks and other objects toward a California Highway Patrol (CHP) patrol vehicle parked below.

FORMER MARINE GETS 100 YEARS IN PRISON AS JUDGE CALLS ICE DETENTION CENTER AMBUSH 'AN ASSAULT ON DEMOCRACY'

Court records show Vega repeatedly helped others ignite debris before setting a large piece of cardboard on fire himself. He then held the burning cardboard over the railing, lined it up with the hood of the CHP vehicle and dropped it onto the cruiser.

As the cardboard burned, Yachua Mauricio Flores, 23, poured a liquid onto the flames, causing the fire to grow as Vega stood nearby and gestured toward the blaze, according to prosecutors.

Vega also admitted throwing multiple rocks at officers as they attempted to clear the overpass. He acknowledged that the burning debris and other objects created a substantial risk of death or serious bodily injury to the officers below.

VIDEO SHOWS MOMENT CHICAGO MAN ALLEGEDLY USED SUV AS WEAPON AGAINST ICE AGENT, PROSECUTORS SAY

"This civil disorder stood apart in its magnitude," federal prosecutors wrote in a sentencing memorandum.

Prosecutors cited a statement from a CHP sergeant with nearly three decades in law enforcement who described the impact the attack had on him and his son.

"His experience underscores how violent this incident became and the deep toll it took on all law enforcement present," prosecutors wrote.

The attack unfolded two days after violence erupted against federal agents carrying out immigration enforcement operations in Los Angeles.

TRUMP ADMINISTRATION HAS LOST OR ABANDONED HUNDREDS OF LAWSUITS AGAINST ANTI-ICE PROTESTERS, MIGRANTS: REPORT

Federal prosecutors previously charged seven people in the overpass attack.

According to court documents, Vega, Flores and Adam Charles Palermo, 40, helped drop burning debris toward the CHP vehicle while others threw rocks at officers trying to clear the overpass.

Vega is the fifth person sentenced in the case.

Flores is scheduled to be sentenced Aug. 3 and faces up to five years in federal prison.

Palermo, whom prosecutors identified as the lead person charged in the case, is scheduled to be sentenced Dec. 14 after pleading guilty to assaulting, resisting and impeding people assisting federal officers with a deadly or dangerous weapon. He faces up to 20 years in prison.

CBP INTERCEPTED BIOLOGICAL MATERIALS TIED TO US–CHINA VIRUS NETWORK BEFORE COVID, NEW DOCUMENTS SHOW

RAND PAUL SEEKS CONTEMPT CHARGES AFTER FAUCI INVOKES FIFTH AMENDMENT MORE THAN 100 TIMES

item.title: Paul Finebaum eviscerates Illinois' Bret Bielema after his claim that the SEC is stuck living in the past
item.description: Paul Finebaum fired back at Bret Bielema's SEC jab at Big Ten media days, calling him the 'village idiot' and citing his conference record at Arkansas.
item.content:encoded:
ESPN's Paul Finebaum has offered a rebuttal to Bret Bielema and the Illinois head coach's nonchalant yet noteworthy comments about the SEC wanting to live in the past. Finebaum brought out the receipts, too, which don't exactly put Bielema in the best light.

While speaking at Big Ten media days on Tuesday, Bielema elected to take a not-so-subtle shot at the Southeastern Conference.

"[SEC commissioner] (Greg) Sankey, I know he's gotta protect the SEC, and they kinda wanna live in 2005 forever," Bielema said while at the podium. "But, I think the forward thinking of where we are in college football is an awesome thing."

ILLINOIS COACH BRET BIELEMA FIRES BACK AT NOTRE DAME AD OVER RECENT REMARKS: 'JUST JOIN A CONFERENCE'

There is absolutely no valid argument to be had against the fact that the Big Ten sits on the throne of college football at the moment with programs from the conference winning three straight national championships. Sure, the SEC won the four before the Big Ten built its recent run, but in today's reality, the Big Ten reigns supreme.

That, however, isn't what Bielema said, he elected to take a jab at the SEC as a whole, which includes some of the most rabid fan bases in all of sports, for being stuck looking into the rearview mirror.

The exact comments from Bielema are rather rich given the fact that he has a history of coaching in the SEC, which Finebaum was quick to remind people of in his response to the head coach.

"He never fails to be the village idiot at Big Ten Media Days," Finebaum said during ESPN's 'Get Up' on Wednesday. "I have no earthly idea where that came from, why he said it. First of all, 2005, since that moment in time, the SEC has only won 13 national championships.

"Let’s go back to Bret Bielema in the SEC at Arkansas. He didn’t make it. His last year, he was 1-8 in the SEC. His overall record in the SEC is 11-29. He was a complete and total disaster. But he always shows up there and gives us something to laugh about, but mostly to laugh at him."

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST SPORTS NEWS

ARKANSAS ATHLETIC DIRECTOR HUNTER YURACHEK DEMANDS SEC CHANGE GAME TIMES FOR RAZORBACKS' FOOTBALL TEAM

Finebaum did make an error during his rebuttal.

Bielema wasn't 1-8 in the SEC during his final season with the Razorbacks. He was actually 1-7, for whatever that is worth. His final campaign with the Hogs at 4-8 in 2017 did come on the heels of three straight winning seasons, but Bielema never came close to meeting expectations in Fayetteville during his five-year tenure, winning just 11 conference games.

item.title: Giants outfielder suffers late-night scooter accident while already dealing with foot injury, team says
item.description: Harrison Bader's scooter accident further injured his foot as the San Francisco Giants outfielder prepares for an MRI while already battling plantar fasciitis.
item.content:encoded:
Harrison Bader's season has gone from bad to worse.

The San Francisco Giants outfielder has been limited to just 30 games due to injury, and when he's been on the field, it has not been pleasant.

Bader is hitting just .170 with a .198 on-base percentage and .358 slugging percentage, as he's dealt with plantar fasciitis for the second time in his MLB career.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

But this week, the Giants announced that Bader had a "scooter accident" on "Saturday night/early Sunday morning," which further injured his foot.

Bader is now set to get an MRI for the new injury.

Bizarrely enough, this is not the first time Bader has gotten into trouble with a scooter. While playing for the University of Florida in 2014, he was suspended for 19 games for drunkenly crashing a scooter into a parked truck.

MLB PROSPECT PROVIDES POSITIVE UPDATES AFTER FRACTURING VERTABRAE IN SCARY OUTFIELD COLLISION

Bader is in the first year of a two-year pact with the Giants, which is worth north of $20 million. The Giants are his seventh team.

The 2021 Gold Glove Award winner spent nearly six full seasons with the St. Louis Cardinals before being traded to the New York Yankees in 2022. He then had a brief stint with the Cincinnati Reds before spending time with the New York Mets, Minnesota Twins and Philadelphia Phillies.

The Giants, meanwhile, are tied for the second-worst record in the National League and figure to trade just about anyone they can ahead of next week's deadline.

item.title: Vacation paradise evacuated as raging wildfire threatens to roar back amid high winds
item.description: Strong winds threaten to reignite the Paros wildfire as tourists and residents share firsthand evacuation accounts from the popular Greek island.
item.content:encoded:
Greek authorities warned Wednesday that strong winds could reignite a wildfire on the popular tourist island of Paros, after the blaze forced residents and visitors to evacuate.

Paros, an island between Mykonos and Santorini, was hit by the wildfire Tuesday, prompting precautionary evacuations in multiple communities.

Flames spread through dry vegetation near the Kampi area, Italian outlet Ansa reported.

THOUSANDS SWARM STUNNING MOUNTAIN ESCAPE AS SELFIE TOURISM BACKLASH ERUPTS ONLINE

Although the blaze has since been largely contained, authorities are warning that strong winds could reignite lingering hot spots, the Greek City Times reported.

The winds could complicate firefighting efforts, the outlet said, and residents are being urged to avoid any activities that could spark fires.

As firefighters battled the blaze, local officials asked residents with available space to help house emergency crews working to contain the fire.

"The Municipality of Paros warmly thanks everyone who is responding in person at this difficult moment, supporting the forces that are fighting the flames." the translated statement read.

MAJOR CITY LAUNCHES HARSH TOURIST CRACKDOWN AS LOCALS REVOLT OVER MASSIVE CROWDS

Fox News Digital reached out to the Municipality of Paros for comment.

Known for its whitewashed villages and beaches, as well as its high-quality Parian marble, the island attracts visitors across the world. 

On a Reddit forum dedicated to travel in Greece, users shared concerns and firsthand accounts of evacuations as the wildfire spread across Paros.

The commenters had been staying in Aliki and Parikia, two villages on the island, as well as the nearby island of Antiparos.

"We were staying near Aliki and had to evacuate," one person said. "Fire is pretty big now."

"I’m in Parikia at the moment. There are currently 4 choppers helping with the [wildfire], plus ground support," another Reddit user said. "They were filling up water right in front of the harbor and flew overhead my hotel."

A third Reddit user said, "We’re in Antiparos now and it’s safe here. We could see the fires from our house last night. It looked really bad, but it seems like it’s almost gone now."

The Paros wildfire comes as Europe continues to battle a severe wildfire season.

Earlier this month, another major wildfire burned near Thessaloniki, Greece's second-largest city, due to record heat and dry conditions.

France and Spain have been hit by massive blazes in recent weeks, including the famed Fontainebleau Forest near Paris, where roughly 4,900 acres of woodland was burned.

While record-breaking heat has intensified the fire danger across Europe, experts say human activity, suspected arson and land management have also contributed to the devastating wildfire season.
